title: pengumon
description: Network monitor: probes, modem / router polling, host services, and pengumon's own health.

panels.title: Network status
panels.description: The classifier's current verdict for the whole path (same as the dashboard banner).

panels.title: Probe loop age
panels.description: Seconds since the 1 s probe loop last finished a round, as of the last export (every 30 s). Growing: the loop is stuck. 'Not exporting': pengumon is down or cannot reach the collector.

panels.title: Incidents opened
panels.description: Network incidents the classifier opened in the selected range.

panels.title: Failed device polls
panels.description: Modem / router polls that failed in the selected range (any error type).

panels.title: HTTP 5xx
panels.description: Server errors answered by the API in the selected range.

panels.title: Errors logged
panels.description: Log lines at ERROR or above in the selected range (Loki).

panels.title: Starts
panels.description: Process starts seen in the selected range (each start is a new instance). More than one: deploys, crashes or reboots; the log shows which.

panels.title: p95 probe latency, by target
panels.description: 95th percentile round-trip time of answered probes. Hops are in path order: local (router), gateway (modem), isp, public, dns. The first hop whose latency jumps is where the problem starts.

panels.title: Probe loss, by target
panels.description: Share of probes without an answer. Loss on every hop from one point on: the fault is at that hop; loss on one middle hop only: often that hop deprioritising ping replies.

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (target) (increase(pengumon_probes_total{job="$service", result="lost"}[$__interval])) or 0 * sum by (target) (increase(pengumon_probes_total{job="$service"}[$__interval]))) / sum by (target) (increase(pengumon_probes_total{job="$service"}[$__interval]))

panels.title: Device polls, by outcome
panels.description: ok: every reading; partial: some capability missing (the log says which); error: the poll failed; unconfigured: no credentials.

panels.title: Failed polls, by error type
panels.description: unreachable / timeout: the device did not answer; auth: the login was refused (check the credentials); protocol: it answered something unexpected; internal: a driver bug (stack trace in the log).

panels.title: p95 poll duration, by device
panels.description: Includes logins. A device that slows down before it fails shows here first; the slow polls' HTTP exchanges are in the traces below.

panels.title: Device status
panels.description: The device snapshot's status: warning / critical judge the readings (signal levels, CPU, memory); error means pengumon could not read the device at all.

targets.expr: max by (device) (pengumon_device_status{job="$service", status="warning"}) * 1 + max by (device) (pengumon_device_status{job="$service", status="critical"}) * 2 + max by (device) (pengumon_device_status{job="$service", status="error"}) * 3 + max by (device) (pengumon_device_status{job="$service", status="unconfigured"}) * 4

panels.title: Probe round duration
panels.description: Time one probe round takes across all targets. Near the 1 s line, rounds start late and the loop age grows.

panels.title: Database writes
panels.description: Probe samples are committed in batches. A slow flush (disk, lock contention) delays everything that reads the database.

panels.title: API requests, by route and status
panels.description: Health checks, static files and credential routes are not recorded.

panels.title: Memory (resident)
panels.description: Resident memory of the pengumon process. A line that climbs and never falls back is a leak.

panels.title: CPU used
panels.description: CPU the pengumon process uses, in cores, split into user and system time.

panels.title: Threads, descriptors, tasks
panels.description: Threads and open file descriptors of the process, and asyncio tasks. Any of the three growing without end is a leak.

panels.title: Event-loop lag
panels.description: How much later than asked a 0.5 s sleep of the event loop woke. Over 0.25 s for two seconds logs a warning (Loki: "Event loop running late").

panels.title: Probe round work, by step
panels.description: What pengumon itself spends in a round after the probes were answered (p95): storing, classifying and building the live message. Separate from probe round-trip time.

panels.title: Late and skipped probe rounds
panels.description: Rounds that started more than 1.5 intervals after the one before: overran = the round before took too long, starved = the event loop was busy. Skipped = rounds that should have run.

panels.title: DNS lookups past their timeout
panels.description: System-resolver lookups still running after the probe gave up on them. Each holds a thread until the resolver returns.

panels.title: Sample buffer
panels.description: Probe samples waiting in memory for the next commit (about 12 a second, flushed every 10 s). It only grows past that while writes fail; at 10 000 the oldest are dropped.

panels.title: Flush failures
panels.description: Commits of the sample buffer that failed, by error type (disk full, read-only volume, locked file).

panels.title: Database and WAL size
panels.description: Size of the SQLite file and its write-ahead log.

panels.title: Retention
panels.description: Rows the hourly retention removed, by table, and the free pages the incremental vacuum returned.

panels.title: Live clients
panels.description: Dashboards connected to the live stream.

panels.title: Live message size and send time
panels.description: Bytes of one live message (p95), and the time to send it to one dashboard (p95).

panels.title: Clients dropped
panels.description: Dashboards disconnected because a send failed: timeout = the client stopped reading, error = it was gone.

panels.title: Rate-limit refusals
panels.description: Requests answered 429 by a rate limit, by bucket.

panels.title: History answer size
panels.description: Rows (p95) and body bytes (p95) of history answers, by endpoint.

panels.title: History answers cut by a cap
panels.description: Answers that hit the row cap, or whose unbucketed range was bucketed or shortened (range), by endpoint.

panels.title: Polls the gate held back
panels.description: Polls a device's minimum-interval gate did not let through, by device and reason: min_interval (a caller got the latest reading), credentials_floor, gate_wait (the schedule waited), auth_stopped (a refused login stopped the schedule).

panels.title: Failures in a row and backoff
panels.description: Consecutive failed polls, and how much longer than its interval a device is now waited for.

panels.title: Rebuilds and background-task exits
panels.description: Devices the supervisor built or dropped after a saved change (reason), gate handovers, and background tasks that died of an exception (any is a bug).

panels.title: Discovery runs
panels.description: Runs by trigger (manual, daily, incident, confirm) and outcome (done, no_answer = no trace reached a public server, failed, cancelled).

panels.title: Discovery and traceroute time
panels.description: p95 time of a discovery run, by trigger, and of one traceroute.

panels.title: Route changes
panels.description: Changes a route-change check saw (found) and the repeat run confirmed, by kind.

panels.title: Alerts by outcome
panels.description: What became of each alert: sent or failed per channel; held (quiet hours), delayed, dropped (a rule) or suppressed (repeat window) before any channel.

panels.title: Alert queue and delivery time
panels.description: Alerts waiting for their time, and p95 delivery time per channel.

panels.title: Settings saves
panels.description: Saves by source and outcome (saved, invalid, conflict, secrets_failed), and settings files read for import.

panels.title: Live-apply failures
panels.description: Settings appliers that raised after a save (the change then waits for a restart), by applier. The error log names the applier and the setting keys.

panels.title: Previews
panels.description: Outage-rules previews by outcome (done, cap = stopped at the time limit, cancelled, failed, busy), and the p95 time and replayed rounds of the finished ones.

panels.title: Warnings and errors
panels.description: Repeated failures are logged once, then as a reminder every 15 minutes, and recovery is logged with the outage's length.

panels.title: Failed operations
panels.description: Spans that ended in an error: failed device polls (with the HTTP exchange that failed), failed requests, path traces. Click a trace id for the whole trace.

panels.title: Slow operations (over 2 s)
panels.description: Device polls, path traces and requests that took more than 2 seconds (open dashboard connections, WS /ws, are left out: they last as long as the page is open).

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: The OTEL_SERVICE_NAME of the pengumon instance to show (default pengumon)
